title: Reel two and the Crescent City Jazz Band at Tommy Thomas's
summary: Second reel opens; the group played as the Crescent City Jazz Band and Loyacano as de facto leader.

blocks.x: You mentioned a couple that I had completely forgotten about. This is September the 29th, 1956. We're at 815 Eileen Street, New Orleans, Louisiana. An informal interview with Mr. Arnold Iacana. This is real two. Continue. Now, Arnold, we were just about beginning to talk about when you had, uh, brought these bunch of boys up from New Orleans to play, uh, when there's a bunch of skip town on you. Yeah. Yeah. Well, uh, you say you played there about a year and a half? Uh, that was Tommy Thomas's,

yes. What did you all call yourself? Well, the Crescent City Jazz Band. Uh-huh. From New Orleans, of Crescent City. You were the leader? Oh, leader. What such a leader as he was. Everybody was a leader. Played a double, huh? No, no. I was just a guy that coaxed all the trouble onto myself and, uh, got in between the boss and the band. I was in the middle all the time. They, uh, for a while everything was great. Then he wanted a raise. I went to the boss and tried to get a raise and I couldn't. Oh, then we should look for another job. Or we should look for another job. And I was the guy that had to get up, watch out there. I was the guy that had to get up in the morning and look for another job for them. Cold freezing mornings and everything else and getting nothing out of it. So I figured, well, shucks, I'm not, I'm not going to get up and look for jobs either. So the band drifted apart. They worked at, uh, uh, Mickey Frank's tile bar. That was a place on, uh, on Clark street and Ohio. Clark and Ohio. Well, we had a good job there. Everything was going great. All right. Yeah, everything was going great until the guy started. They, they, we used to operate on Sunday, Sunday night. Of course, it was against the law, but you know, they used to operate anyhow. And they had a service bar, a special service bar. And up above that special service bar, they had, uh, some cupboards up there loaded with whiskey. And they had a hair spa on the thing.
